## Welcome

This website accompanies the manuscript "*scDiagnostics: systematic assessment of cell type annotation in single-cell transcriptomics data*" (Christidis et al., in review). 

It provides comprehensive tutorials, analysis code, and reproducible workflows demonstrating how [`scDiagnostics`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/scDiagnostics) can evaluate and diagnose automated cell type annotations across different single-cell technologies and biological contexts.

## Overview

We showcase `scDiagnostics` using two distinct public datasets:

- **COVID-19 PBMC scRNA-seq** (~48,000 query cells): Dense, high-cell-count dataset diagnosing annotations from severe COVID-19 infection vs. healthy controls. Shows how annotation methods handle disease-driven transcriptomic shifts.

- **MERFISH Mouse Colitis** (~29,000 query cells): Spatial transcriptomics dataset evaluating annotations in DSS-induced inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Demonstrates performance on targeted gene panels and spatial information.

For each dataset, we generate annotations using four popular tools and compare their performance:

- [**Azimuth**](https://github.com/satijalab/azimuth) — Weighted k-NN mapping
- [**SingleR**](https://bioconductor.org/packages/SingleR) — Correlation-based assignment
- [**CellTypist**](https://www.celltypist.org/) — Machine learning classifier
- [**scVI/scArches**](https://docs.scvi-tools.org/) — Deep learning with VAE

## Key Findings

- **Annotation methods show substantial agreement** on major cell types but diverge on rare/inflamed populations
- **Anomaly detection identifies transcriptomically divergent cells** that correlate with disease state
- **Inflamed fibroblasts are frequently misclassified** as smooth muscle cells, particularly by distance-based methods
- **Confidence scores alone are insufficient** — need complementary diagnostics like anomaly detection
